central_question: What will the November 3, 2026 US midterm elections produce in terms of House and Senate control, including which party wins each chamber and the magnitude of seat gains or losses?

situation_brief.current_situation: With Election Day 122 days away, the 2026 midterm environment is structurally Democratic-leaning: Trump's job approval sits in the mid-to-high 30s (37% AP-NORC, 36% Reuters/Ipsos, 38% Marquette, 43% Harvard CAPS/Harris), the generic ballot reads D+5 to D+7, and 2025-2026 congressional special-election overperformance has averaged D+17.1. The Cook Political Report has shifted 4 Senate races toward Democrats in its single-largest one-sided move this cycle (NC and GA to Lean D, OH-special to Toss-Up, NE to Likely R); Sabato's Crystal Ball on June 11 added AK to Toss-Up alongside NC and OH-special. The Cook analyst's central estimate is '1 to 3 seat Democratic pickup, just short of 4' needed for a Senate majority. House: 17 of 435 toss-up seats per the April 7 update, with Republicans defending 14 of them. The June 17 Iran ceasefire has stabilized — but not recovered — Trump's approval, leaving the structural environment intact for the next four months.
situation_brief.context: Donald Trump returned to office in January 2025; by April 2026 his approval had collapsed to a record 33-34% low as effective tariff rates peaked near 28% (Yale Budget Lab) and an unanticipated 3.5-month war with Iran (Feb 28 – Jun 17, 2026) imposed roughly $1,500-2,500 per-household tariff costs plus an unpopular war footing. Partial recovery followed: tariffs dialed back to a 16.8% effective rate (down from 28% peak), gas prices eased as the Strait of Hormuz reopened, and a Jun 17 ceasefire ended combat — but 53% (AP-NORC) say Iran military action went 'too far' and 54% (Economist/YouGov) say going to war was the wrong decision, so the public has not rewarded Trump for ending an unpopular war. The cumulative effect has been Democratic underdog overperformances in congressional specials, a historically reliable leading indicator of the House majority.
situation_brief.dynamics: The principal tension is between a structural Democratic-leaning environment (Trump 35-37% approval, D+5 to D+7 generic ballot, D+17 special-election overperformance) and asymmetric chamber math — Democrats need a net of 4 Senate seats but the Lean D + Toss-Up seats total only 6-7, leaving no margin for error. The Iranian ceasefire is fragile: fire was traded across the Strait of Hormuz the weekend of June 27-29; the 60-day interim expires mid-August. The Supreme Court is the single biggest unknown variable: a ruling on NRSC v. FEC could neutralize the DCCC's $45.3M cycle-record cash lead, while the IEEPA tariff case (expected December 2026) could halve the effective tariff rate if SCOTUS strikes IEEPA tariffs. Trump announced a first-of-its-kind midterm convention (Sept 9-10 Dallas) to rally the GOP base — historically analog conventions (1994 'Contract with America,' 2010 'Pledge to America') preceded R+54 and R+63 House waves, but those were offensive rather than defensive relaunches. The base-case trajectory is for a modest D House wave (75-85% probability) and Rs holding the Senate by 1-3 seats (65-78% probability).

contested_claims.claim: Generic ballot D+ advantage between D+3 (CNN/Enten) and D+7 (USPollingData / Silver Bulletin)
contested_claims.why_they_differ: Different pollster weightings; LV vs. RV screening; with/without 'Republican control' question framing. Silver Bulletin is methodology-conservative; USPollingData is the open-ended figure.

contested_claims.claim: Trump approval rating ranges from 33% (UMass progressive-house outlier) to 43% (Harvard CAPS/Harris pro-R outlier) with consensus 35-37%
contested_claims.why_they_differ: House effects differ: UMass has progressive lean; Harvard CAPS/Harris has slight Republican lean. Reuters/Ipsos and AP-NORC (the cleanest) cluster at 35-37%.

contested_claims.claim: Ohio Senate special-election poll lead — Democrats cite Fabrizio/Anzalone D+3; Republicans cite Nexstar/Emerson R+6
contested_claims.why_they_differ: Different pollster house effects; Fabrizio/Anzalone is a Democratic-aligned pollster with R-favorable shift; Nexstar/Emerson is a partisan-Republican-pollster with similar house effect. Split poll signals a coin-flip race.

contested_claims.claim: Maine Senate — Collins R+3 topline but Platner +9 among 'extremely motivated' voters

sources: Nate Silver All-In June 23 ME at 50-50

contested_claims.why_they_differ: Methodological: 'extremely motivated' subgroup is a turnout-indicator; top-line is full-LV. Platinum candidate baggage and Dem turnout uncertainty both affect the final election outcome. Silver calls ME '50-50 coin flip'.

contested_claims.claim: Iran ceasefire durability — currently 60-day interim ceasefire (signed June 17); fire traded weekend of June 27-29; risk of collapse by mid-August
contested_claims.why_they_differ: 60-day interim deadline mid-August is the binary trigger; Strait of Hormuz 'fire-traded' weekend of June 27-29 already indicates fragility; either direction is a ±3-5 pt swing in Trump approval.
